# `⇄` — Minimize

Keys: `Alt-4`

`cost⇄ start` searches for the point where the function `cost` gives its least value, starting from `start`, and returns that point. `start` is a number or an array of real numbers, and the point has its shape and keys. `cost` takes a point and gives one real number.

```bpl
{⊼⍵-2}⇄ 10   ⍝ 2
```

The point is approximate. A search stops when its steps change the value by less than option `tolerance`, relative to the value. For 64-bit floats the default is about `1.5E¯8`. Rosenbrock's function has its least value at `1 1`. With a smaller tolerance, the search finds that point to nearly full precision:

```bpl
rosen←{[x y]←⍵ ⋄ ⊼1-x + 100×⊼y-⊼x}
["tolerance":1E¯14] rosen⇄ ¯1.2 1   ⍝ 1 1
```

A keyed left argument gives the options. Option `method` chooses the method. Without it, `⇄` chooses from the start, from whether there are bounds and from whether `cost` has a derivative:

| `method` | Method | Chosen when |
|---|---|---|
| `"brent"` | Brent's method, along one variable | the start is one number |
| `"l-bfgs"` | L-BFGS, which follows the derivative | `cost` has a derivative and there are no bounds |
| `"powell"` | Powell's method of conjugate directions | there are bounds |
| `"nelder-mead"` | Nelder–Mead's simplex | none of the above apply |
| `"differential-evolution"` | differential evolution, which evolves a population of points across the bounds | only when named |

`cost` has a derivative where [`f∂`](derivative.qmd) differentiates it: a bound polynomial evaluator, or a function with a derivative that `f∂←g` attaches. L-BFGS calls `f∂` at each point where it needs the gradient, which holds one number for each variable. Nelder–Mead and Powell's method use only values of `cost`. Differential evolution suits a function with many local minima, and needs finite bounds.

```bpl
rosen←{[x y]←⍵ ⋄ ⊼1-x + 100×⊼y-⊼x}
rosen∂←{⍺←1 ⋄ [x y]←⍵ ⋄ ⍺×[(¯2×1-x) - 400×x×y-⊼x; 200×y-⊼x]}
["tolerance":1E¯14] rosen⇄ ¯1.2 1   ⍝ 1 1
```

| Option | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | the method, from the table above | chosen as the table shows |
| `lower`, `upper` | the least and greatest value of each variable: one number for every variable, or an array with the start's shape and keys | no bound, as `¯∞` and `∞` give |
| `tolerance` | the relative change at which the method stops | the square root of the working floats' machine epsilon |
| `evaluations` | the most calls of `cost` | 1000 for each variable, plus 1000, and for differential evolution another 1000 for each member of its population |
| `population` | the number of points differential evolution evolves | 15 for each variable, and at least 5 |
| `seed` | the seed of differential evolution's random choices | 0 |
| `batch` | whether to call `cost` once on several points | `$f` |
| `report` | whether to give a record of the search's results | `$f` |

Each method evaluates `cost` only within the bounds, starting from the start moved inside them.

```bpl
rosen←{[x y]←⍵ ⋄ ⊼1-x + 100×⊼y-⊼x}
["lower":[¯∞ 0] "upper":[0.8 ∞]] rosen⇄ 0.5 0.5   ⍝ 0.8 0.64
```

A record of named parameters makes a natural start, and the point keeps its keys. Bounds can be records with the same keys.

```bpl
cost←{(⊼⍵.gap-6) + ⊼⍵.margin-2×⍵.gap}
["lower":["gap":0 "margin":0]] cost⇄ ["gap":8 "margin":12]   ⍝ ["gap":6 "margin":12]
```

Where `batch` is true, `⇄` calls `cost` once for the points a method evaluates together: Nelder–Mead's first simplex and each shrink of it, and each generation of differential evolution. The points lie along a new last axis of the start's shape, and `cost` gives a vector with one value for each point. Each field of a record start then holds one value per point. Arithmetic on fields works on a batch as it does on one point. A `cost` that reduces over a vector start with `+/` needs `+⌿` on a batch.

```bpl
cost←{(⊼⍵.gap-6) + ⊼⍵.margin-2×⍵.gap}
lo←["gap":0 "margin":0] ⋄ hi←["gap":20 "margin":40]
["method":"differential-evolution" "lower":lo "upper":hi "batch":$t] cost⇄ ["gap":8 "margin":12]
⍝ ["gap":6 "margin":12]
```

Where `report` is true, the result is a record. Field `x` holds the point, `value` holds `cost` at the point, `evaluations` counts the calls of `cost`, and `converged` says whether the method's stopping test passed before the calls reached `evaluations`. The point is the best one the search evaluated, whether or not it converged.

```bpl
r←["evaluations":10 "report":$t] {+/⊼⍵-3}⇄ 1 2
[r.evaluations r.converged]   ⍝ 10ₓ $f
```

The search works in floats of the start's width. 32-bit and 16-bit floats compute in 32 bits, and exact numbers become floats of the default width. A `cost` of NaN counts as greater than every number.

Errors: `LENGTH` for bounds of another shape or other keys, a derivative that doesn't give one number for each variable, or a batched `cost` that doesn't give one value for each point; `DOMAIN` for an unknown option or method, a start or bound that isn't real numbers, a lower bound above its upper bound, a `cost` that doesn't give one real number, `"brent"` with more than one variable, `"l-bfgs"` with no derivative or with bounds, `"differential-evolution"` without finite bounds or with a population below 4, a `tolerance` that isn't positive, or an `evaluations`, `population` or `seed` that isn't a whole number.
